reasoning_trace: This fault type is labeled cross_domain/cascade, so per the project's own known history these can have a confounding secondary symptom that outshines the real root -- traced more payments than usual across the full 30s window specifically to check for that, not just accepting the first signal. Witness monitor: settlement DOWN then RECOVERED, generated independently with no foreknowledge. Traced 8 payments spanning the entire window. All 8 show the identical pattern: gateway PAYMENT_SUBMITTED, validation-enrichment PAYMENT_VALIDATED (one payment, a7967033, got a legitimate business PAYMENT_REJECTED at validation -- not a stall, a real outcome), aml-compliance AML_SCREENING_COMPLETE, routing-execution RAIL_SELECTED and PAYMENT_ROUTED, fraud-scoring FRAUD_SCORE_COMPUTED (independent of the sequential chain, as established in earlier cases) -- and then nothing further. None of the 8 show a SETTLEMENT_COMPLETE event. Unlike what the cascade/confounded label might suggest, no other service shows any anomaly here: routing-execution's RAIL_SELECTED and PAYMENT_ROUTED fire promptly and normally for every payment, aml-compliance clears every payment quickly, validation-enrichment shows no unusual latency. The stall is clean and specific to settlement, matching the DB_TIMEOUT case's pattern exactly (same root service, same evidentiary shape). Conclusion reached from evidence alone, before reading the injector's own log: settlement.
confirmation_basis: Blind conclusion (settlement) matches the injector's own ground-truth log exactly. Corroborated by both the independent health witness and a consistent payment-funnel stall boundary across 8 traced payments spanning the full window -- deliberately checked more payments than usual given this fault type's 'cascade' label, and found no misleading secondary symptom in this particular run.
